gates.reason: Unit-test fixtures perform no authentication, I/O, egress, command execution, or browser rendering.
Inspected assertions covering evidence labels, fail-closed exclusion joins, deterministic specs, survivor-only clustering, and serialized handoffs.
Test-only code is not shipped or executed on a production hot path.
Pure client-side preparation performs no filesystem writes, LLM/network egress, command execution, secret access, or unsafe HTML construction.
Exclusions are joined by runId, ambiguous joins fail closed, only kept records reach clusters, counts are derived from final rows, and proposed specs are validated before handoff.
Dataset preparation uses bounded linear passes and indexed maps; no request fan-out, repeated parsing, or obvious superlinear hot-path work was found.
Unit tests contain only in-memory fixtures and assertions with no privileged or browser-facing operations.
Tests cover stable IDs, deterministic ordering, normalization scope, threshold boundaries, unprofiled fallbacks, malformed input, deduplication, and recomputed counts.
Test-only code is outside the shipped runtime path.
The raw-cluster parser bounds identifier lengths and run counts, validates enums and shapes, and exposes no execution, HTML, filesystem, or network sink.
Cluster axes are deterministically derived from observable run fields, fixed token bands, documented normalization, stable tie-breaking, and validated member identifiers.
Clustering is linear apart from sorting output members; raw run lists are capped at 500 and no per-request I/O or recomputation loop was found.
Unit-test fixtures and assertions do not exercise a security-sensitive runtime surface.
Assertions recheck all six exclusion classes, threshold boundaries, partial-data coverage language, signal arithmetic, and sanitizer round-tripping.
Test-only code does not run in the production ingest or rendering path.
Command text is only compared as inert lowercase data against caller-supplied patterns; it is never executed, rendered as HTML, written, or transmitted.

Each classifier cites measured fields in its reason, arithmetic and thresholds were re-derived, unavailable classifiers are explicitly disclosed, and reasons are length-bounded for schema preservation.
Signal construction indexes related datasets once and processes sessions and events linearly without nested whole-dataset scans.
Unit tests use inert typed fixtures with no auth, filesystem, network, command, or rendering behavior.
Tests verify ranking direction, evidence-strength demotion, score limits, candidate caps, cost construction, durations, turns, and error counts, though they do not cover mixed-model sessions.
Test-only code is not part of a runtime hot path.
The miner is pure over already-parsed records and performs no LLM egress, secret access, filesystem writes, command execution, or browser rendering.
A session is attributed to its first resolvable model while cost, tokens, duration, and failures are aggregated across every model used in that session.
Mining performs a fixed number of linear passes plus candidate sorting and caps returned candidates; no I/O or N× related-data lookup was found.

findings.title: Mixed-model sessions misattribute whole-session evidence to the first model
findings.where: src/lib/model-gap-mining.ts:184 selects the first resolvable model; src/lib/model-gap-mining.ts:225 aggregates cost and tokens from every entry; src/lib/model-gap-mining.ts:238 attaches whole-session duration and error totals to that selected model.
findings.what: For a session that changes models, the emitted candidate's modelId, family, and direction describe only the first resolvable entry, while its cost proxy, token count, duration, tool errors, and API errors describe the entire session. This can reproducibly label a Haiku-to-Sonnet gap using work or failures produced after switching to Sonnet/Opus, so the discovery claim is not evidence-faithful.
findings.fix: Build model-specific run segments and aggregate only entries and attributable signals for each segment, or fail closed by excluding mixed-family sessions with an explicit auditable reason until per-model attribution is available.
findings.acceptance: Add a test with a session whose first entry is Haiku and later entry is Opus with the dominant tokens/cost; verify the miner either emits correctly separated model-scoped evidence or excludes the mixed-family session, and never emits a Haiku-directed candidate carrying the Opus totals.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the mismatch at baseline: sessionFamily returns immediately on the first resolvable entry (lines 184-190), the adapter sums all entries (lines 225-231), and then combines those totals with session-wide timing/errors under that first model (lines 238-249). No mixed-model guard or segmentation exists in the audited file.
